natural_language: Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory (finite case). Let E/F be a finite Galois extension. There is an inclusion-reversing bijection between intermediate fields F ⊆ K ⊆ E and subgroups of the Galois group Gal(E/F), sending K to the subgroup of automorphisms fixing K, and a subgroup H to its fixed field.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Basic
/-- Finite Galois correspondence: intermediate fields ↔ subgroups of the Galois group. -/
theorem finite_galois_correspondence
    {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] [IsGalois F E] [FiniteDimensional F E] :
    -- The order-reversing equivalence is IntermediateField.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup
    Nonempty (
      IntermediateField F E ≃o (Subgroup (E ≃ₐ[F] E))ᵒᵈ) :=
  ⟨IntermediateField.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup⟩

natural_language: Primitive element theorem. A finite separable field extension E/F is simple: there exists α ∈ E such that E = F(α).
lean_code:
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.PrimitiveElement
theorem exists_primitive_element
    {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
    [FiniteDimensional F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] :
    ∃ α : E, F⟮α⟯ = ⊤ :=
  Field.exists_primitive_element F E

natural_language: Cayley–Hamilton theorem. For any square matrix A over a commutative ring, the characteristic polynomial of A annihilates A: χ_A(A) = 0.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Coeff
theorem cayley_hamilton
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {n : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n R) :
    A.charpoly.aeval A = 0 :=
  Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly A

natural_language: Banach fixed-point theorem (contraction mapping theorem). A contraction mapping on a nonempty complete metric space has a unique fixed point.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Contracting
theorem contraction_fixed_point
    {α : Type*} [MetricSpace α] [CompleteSpace α] [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → α} {K : ℝ} (hK : K < 1) (hf : LipschitzWith (⟨K, le_of_lt hK⟩) f) :
    ∃! x : α, f x = x := by
  -- Mathlib's ContractingWith API
  have : ContractingWith ⟨K, le_of_lt hK⟩ f := ⟨hf⟩
  exact this.existsUnique_fixedPoint

natural_language: Hahn–Banach theorem (analytic form). A bounded linear functional defined on a subspace of a real normed space extends to the whole space with the same operator norm.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.HahnBanach.Extension
theorem hahn_banach_extension
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {p : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ} {s : Subspace ℝ E} (hp : ∃ M, ∀ x : s, ‖p x‖ ≤ M * ‖x.1‖) :
    ∃ q : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ x : s, q x.1 = p x) ∧
      (∃ M, ∀ x, ‖q x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖) := by
  -- Use Mathlib extension; simplified existence packaging
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := Real.exists_extension_norm_eq s p (Classical.choose_spec hp)
  refine ⟨q, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x; exact hq.1 x
  · exact ⟨‖q‖, fun x => q.le_opNorm x⟩

natural_language: Quadratic reciprocity. For distinct odd primes p and q, the Legendre symbols satisfy (p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^((p-1)(q-1)/4).
lean_code:
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticReciprocity
theorem quadratic_reciprocity
    {p q : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    legendreSym q p * legendreSym p q =
      (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2)) :=
  quadratic_reciprocity hp hq hpq

natural_language: Fundamental theorem of algebra. Every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root. Consequently ℂ is algebraically closed.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.Basic
theorem fundamental_theorem_of_algebra
    {p : Polynomial ℂ} (h : p.degree ≠ 0) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, p.isRoot z :=
  Complex.exists_root h

natural_language: Yoneda lemma. For a locally small category C, the natural transformations from the representable functor Hom(X, –) to a functor F are in bijection with the elements of F(X).
lean_code:

    (yoneda.obj X ⟶ F) ≅ F.obj X :=
  CategoryTheory.Yoneda.yonedaEquiv.toIso  -- shape: use yonedaEquiv API

natural_language: Baire category theorem. A complete metric space is a Baire space: the intersection of countably many dense open sets is dense.
lean_code:

    BaireSpace X :=
  inferInstance

natural_language: Open mapping theorem. A surjective continuous linear map between Banach spaces is an open map.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.BoundedLinearMaps
theorem open_mapping_theorem
    {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    (f : E →L[ℂ] F) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    IsOpenMap f :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap f hf
